items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: He left one morning for Charleston, West Virginia, in a Pierce Arrow owned by a fellow named Richard Carpenter... we could get 10 musicians in it with Rich driving

ctx.x: I went to the theatre where Doc was playing and to my surprise he was playing alto sax and trumpet in the show. I never knew who the other musicians were in the group because "Doc" Cheatham was the only one that interested me. The show stayed for two weeks in town and I went to see it and mostly to listen to "Doc" Cheatham at least 8 times.

The first trip out of Cincinnati that I made with Page was a real catastrophe. He left one morning for Charleston, West Virginia, in a Pierce Arrow owned by a fellow named Richard Carpenter. A Pierce Arrow was and still is a wealthy man's car, and how "Rich", as everyone called him, came to own one, I never found out. It was a 7-passenger car but we could get 10 musicians in it with Rich driving and we were not uncomfortable. We were all on the slim side except Edgar James. Also we had our personal baggage, plus…
luggage could be put on the side and on the fender between the hood over the left and right side of the front wheels.
